text.p: These are the leading st ories in the Belgrade press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
NASA BORBA
- Belgrade electoral commission confirms opposition win in Belgrade city council in application of the special law on local elections.
- Belgrade students continue their protest marches, support journalists of state TV channel 3 who were suspended or fired for aligning themselves with the students.
- Teachers protest throughout Serbia demanding outstanding wages. Some 10,000 teachers protest in front of Serbian government on Thursday.
- Workers of one of the trade unions of Zastava car factory in Kragujevac started a strike Thursday, demanding outstanding wages.

- Serb refugees from Bosnia and Croatia living in Yugoslavia express revulsion over Serbian Parliament Speaker Dragan Tomic's description of them as the most militant element among Serbia's demonstrators.

- Ferro-nickel factory in Glogovac, in Serbia's Kosovo province, will get a $2.5 million three-year credit from French firm SMM-Comesim for putting into operation a second furnace for nickel production.
- National Bank of Yugoslavia gives Belgrade's JIK Bank one more month to consolidate itself and promises to reconsider decision on its closure.
- U.S. decides to give $2 million in equipment and supplies to opposition media in Serbia in 1997.
POLITIKA

- Serbian president Slobodan Milosevic receives newly elected government members, urges them to create necessary economic environment to boost expansion of productiont and put the country's resources to best use.
- Yugoslav delegation to hold bilateral meeting with the chief international representative for the succession of the former Yugoslavia in Brussels on February 20.
- Serbia's new education minister Jova Todorovic to meet Belgrade University deans Friday to discuss possibility of making up for classes lost during student protest.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Some 20 km of Danube river bank polluted by oil leak of up to 150 tonnes on January 31.
- The federal government decides to spend 17 percent of its 9.23 million dinar 1997 budget in the first quarter of the year.
BORBA
- International arbitration commission has decided that Brcko should remain in Bosnian Serb republic, say diplomatic sources in Geneva.
- Construction industry claims for work carried out for PTT, Electricity comnpany and municipality stand at 250 million dinars ($45.5 million).
- Montenegro soon to form special foreign investment centre within the scope of its agency for restructuring the economy.
-- Belgrade newsroom, 381 11 222 43 05
